```text
# Board System Quick Reference

> Full specification: `board-system-spec.md`

## File Naming

```
TYPE-NNNN_kebab-case-description.md
```

| Prefix | Type |
|--------|------|
| `TASK` | Task |
| `EPIC` | Epic |
| `ADR` | Architecture Decision Record |
| `REFE` | Reference |
| `RESO` | Resource |
| `NOTE` | Note |

## Document Types

| Type | Status Values | Description |
|------|---------------|-------------|
| `task` | `backlog` → `current` → `done` | Actionable work item |
| `epic` | `planning` → `current` → `done` | Container for related tasks |
| `adr` | `active` \| `superseded` \| `deprecated` | Decision record, written after decision made |
| `reference` | _(none)_ | Evergreen knowledge base (encyclopedic) |
| `resource` | `inbox` → `processing` → `processed` | External material to review |
| `note` | `inbox` → `processed` | Unrefined thoughts (to be refined, then archived) |

## Priority (Tasks)

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `1` | High |
| `2` | Medium |
| `3` | Low |

## Required Frontmatter

**Task:**
```yaml
---
type: task
status: backlog
priority: 2
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

**Epic:**
```yaml
---
type: epic
status: planning
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

**ADR:**
```yaml
---
type: adr
status: active
context_date: YYYY-MM-DD
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

**Resource:**
```yaml
---
type: resource
status: inbox
url: https://example.com
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

**Reference:**
```yaml
---
type: reference
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

**Note:**
```yaml
---
type: note
status: inbox
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

## Directory Structure

```
board/
├── tasks/       # TASK-* files
├── planning/    # EPIC-*, ADR-*, NOTE-* files
├── reference/   # REFE-* files
├── resources/   # RESO-* files
└── archive/     # Completed items (except ADRs — they stay in planning/)
```

## Writing Rules

### Task Titles: Use Imperative Mood

Start with a verb. Describe the action to be done.

| Bad | Good |
|-----|------|
| User Authentication | Add user authentication |
| PNG Compression | Optimize PNG compression |
| Bug in Login | Fix login authentication bug |

### REFE vs ADR

| REFE (Reference) | ADR (Decision Record) |
|------------------|----------------------|
| What things ARE | What WE DID/DECIDED |
| Objective, encyclopedic | Subjective to this project |
| Evergreen, keep current | Immutable, never edited |
| No project decisions | Documents our choices |

### Epics vs Tasks

- **Epic**: Container for related tasks (lives in `planning/`)
- **Task**: Single, completable unit of work (lives in `tasks/`)

If it can't be done in one focused effort, split it into tasks under an epic.

**Quick test:** "Could someone meaningfully complete and ship part of this while the rest remains undone?" If yes → EPIC.

**EPIC signals:** multiple distinct verbs/actions, work spans multiple code areas, sub-steps shippable independently, would produce multiple PRs, description joins separate deliverables with "and".

### NOTE Lifecycle

NOTEs are the "to be refined" inbox. When processed, they **spawn** new artifacts:

```
NOTE (inbox) → process → spawns TASK(s), REFE(s), ADR(s), RESO(s) → archive NOTE (processed)
```

- NOTEs spawn, never convert — the original stays as historical record
- Never delete NOTEs — archive with `status: processed`
- One NOTE can spawn many artifacts, or none
```

7	# Add a "Why Is This Needed" Section That Explains the APOD API
8	
9	Add a section to the landing page that explains what the APOD API is, why it exists, and why a proxy like nasapicture.com is useful.
10	
11	## What to cover
12	
13	- **What is APOD?** — NASA publishes a new Astronomy Picture of the Day every day, with a professional explanation written by astronomers. It's been running since 1995.
14	- **The problem** — NASA's API requires an API key, has rate limits (30 req/hr on DEMO_KEY), sometimes returns videos instead of images, and doesn't offer a single stable URL that always points to "today's image."
15	- **What this solves** — nasapicture.com gives you a fixed URL that always returns today's image. No API key, no rate limits (edge-cached), no video days (auto-fallback). One URL, drop it in an `<img>` tag.
16	
17	## Tone & placement
18	
19	- Keep it concise — a few short paragraphs, not a wall of text. Match the existing voice (clever, minimal, precise).
20	- Place it between the hero image and the developer-facing route docs, so non-technical visitors get context before the technical details.
21	- Consider a heading like "Why does this exist?" or "The problem with APOD" — something that invites curiosity.
22

1	---
2	type: note
3	status: inbox
4	created: 2026-03-31
5	---
6	
7	# Generate a daily OG image
8	
9	Generate a new Open Graph image every day, resized and cropped to the optimal 1200x630px dimensions. Adding a text overlay with the logo would be a bonus.
10	
11	## Context
12	
13	The current OG image points to `https://api.nasapicture.com/image.jpg`, which serves the raw APOD at whatever dimensions NASA provides (often square or portrait). Social platforms expect 1200x630px for optimal previews.
14	
15	## Recommended approach: `workers-og`
16	
17	[`workers-og`](https://github.com/kvnang/workers-og) renders HTML/CSS to PNG entirely inside a Worker (Satori → SVG → PNG, no browser needed). This is purpose-built for OG image generation at the edge.
18	
19	**How it would work:**
20	1. Add a `/og` route to the existing Worker (or a separate one)
21	2. Fetch today's APOD metadata from `/info` (title, date)
22	3. Render an HTML template with the APOD photo as background, title text, and nasapicture.com branding
23	4. Cache the result aggressively (24h TTL keyed to date) — one cold generation per day
24	5. Update the `og:image` meta tag to point to the new `/og` route
25	
26	**Pros:** Single Worker, zero external dependencies, familiar HTML/CSS for layout, no billing (stays within free Workers tier since we're generating the image ourselves, not using Cloudflare's Images API).
27	
28	**Cons:** Satori supports flexbox only (no CSS grid). Custom fonts need to be embedded as ArrayBuffers (adds to bundle size). Subset of CSS supported.
29	
30	## Alternative: Cloudflare Images binding
31	
32	Use the Images binding (`env.IMAGES`) to resize/crop the APOD to 1200x630 natively, then `.draw()` a pre-rendered text overlay PNG on top.
33	
34	- Requires `[images] binding = "IMAGES"` in `wrangler.toml`
35	- Free tier: 5,000 unique transformations/month (we'd use ~30/month — well within limits)
36	- Higher-fidelity resizing with smart crop/gravity options
37	- More moving parts (two-step: resize + composite)
38	
39	This is the upgrade path if `workers-og` quality isn't sufficient or if we need smarter cropping (e.g. face/subject detection).
40	
41	## Not viable
42	
43	- **Sharp** — uses native Node.js modules, incompatible with Workers
44	- **Canvas APIs** — no browser context in Workers
45	
46	## Useful links
47	
48	- [workers-og](https://github.com/kvnang/workers-og)
49	- [@cf-wasm/photon](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cf-wasm/photon) — WASM image processing if more control is needed
50	- [Cloudflare Images: draw overlays](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/transform-images/draw-overlays/)
51	- [Cloudflare Images pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/pricing/) — free up to 5,000 transformations/month
52
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	type: note
3	status: inbox
4	created: 2026-03-31
5	---
6	
7	# Auto-refresh landing page on APOD rollover
8	
9	If a user leaves the landing page open, the image and caption should update automatically when NASA publishes the new APOD — no manual reload required.
10	
11	## Approach: Self-correcting countdown + short-burst polling
12	
13	Two phases: a coarse countdown that converges on midnight ET, then burst polling to catch the exact publish moment.
14	
15	### Phase 1: Countdown
16	
17	On page load, compute the offset between the user's clock and CF server time (from the `/info` response `Date` header). Use this offset to calculate a corrected "time until midnight ET." Run a `setInterval` every 5 minutes that recalculates the remaining time. This self-corrects for:
18	- Long `setTimeout` drift (browsers throttle timers in background tabs)
19	- Tabs hidden for hours or days (each tick recalculates from scratch)
20	- No single long timeout that fires late or not at all
21	
22	When the countdown shows <5 minutes to midnight ET, transition to phase 2.
23	
24	### Phase 2: Burst polling
25	
26	Poll `/info` every 2 minutes, comparing `data.date` to `currentDate`. When the date changes, call `updateApod(data)` and stop polling. Cap at 30 minutes (15 requests max), then re-enter phase 1 and schedule the next midnight.
27	
28	Total requests per rollover: ~15. Total requests the rest of the day: zero.
29	
30	### Sequence
31	
32	1. On page load, store `currentDate` from initial `/info` response
33	2. Compute clock offset from CF `Date` header: `serverTime - localTime`
34	3. Start 5-min `setInterval` that recalculates ms until midnight ET using the offset
35	4. When <5 min remain, clear the interval and start 2-min burst polling
36	5. When `data.date !== currentDate`, call `updateApod(data)`, stop polling, re-enter step 3 for next day
37	6. After 30 min with no date change, stop polling and re-enter step 3
38	7. On `visibilitychange` to visible, do an immediate `/info` check (catches long-hidden tabs)
39	
40	### Image transition on rollover
41	
42	- Fade out current image (remove `.loaded` class)
43	- Fetch new `/thumb`, set as wrapper background
44	- Cache-bust the image by appending the new date: `img.src = \`${API_BASE}/optimized?d=${data.date}\``
45	- Update aspect ratio from new dimensions
46	- On `img.load`, fade back in
47	- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (skip fade, show immediately)
48	- Swap happens regardless of focus mode
49	
50	### Time source: CF `Date` header (preferred)
51	
52	Use the `Date` response header from the initial `/info` fetch as the authoritative time source. This comes from Cloudflare's edge server (NTP-synced), so it's reliable regardless of the user's local clock. Parse it to compute ms until midnight ET, no extra requests needed.
53	
54	```js
55	const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/info`);
56	const serverNow = new Date(res.headers.get('Date'));
57	// compute ms until midnight ET from serverNow
58	```
59	
60	### Alternatives considered
61	
62	**User's local clock** — Could use `new Date()` from the user's machine to compute time until midnight ET. Simpler, but assumes the user's clock is accurate. Rejected because clock skew on user machines is common enough to cause missed or premature rollovers.
63	
64	**External time APIs** — worldtimeapi.org and timeapi.io are free, no-key options. Unnecessary here since we already get authoritative time from the CF `Date` header, but available if we ever need a dedicated time source.
65	
66	### Edge cases
67	
68	- **Browser image cache** — The `/optimized` URL doesn't change day-to-day, so the browser may serve a stale cached image on rollover. Bust it with a date query param: `/optimized?d=2026-04-05`. The Worker ignores query params for routing but the browser treats it as a new URL.
69	- **Multiple rollovers** — After each successful rollover, re-enter the countdown phase for the next midnight. Not a one-time setup.
70	- **Tab hidden for days** — The `visibilitychange` handler does an immediate `/info` check, catching any missed rollovers regardless of how long the tab was hidden.
71	- **Thumb cache busting** — Same browser cache issue as `/optimized` applies to `/thumb`. Append `?d=${data.date}` to the thumb fetch on rollover too.
72	- **Object URL cleanup** — Each rollover creates a new blob URL for the thumbnail via `URL.createObjectURL()`. Revoke the previous one with `URL.revokeObjectURL()` to avoid memory leaks.
73	
74	### Implementation notes
75	
76	- Refactor initial caption/image/thumbnail setup into a reusable `updateApod(data)` function
77	- All changes in `landing/index.html` script block, no Worker changes needed
78	- Cache keys are date-based and roll at midnight ET, so post-midnight `/info` requests will cache-miss for the new date and fetch fresh from NASA
79	- Zero new dependencies
80
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	type: note
3	status: inbox
4	created: 2026-04-01
5	updated: 2026-04-05
6	---
7	
8	# Add GitHub Action to auto-deploy to Cloudflare on PR merge into main
9	
10	Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that runs `npm run deploy` automatically when a PR is merged into `main`. This removes the manual deploy step after each merge.
11	
12	## Current Deploy Process
13	
14	`npm run deploy` runs two steps sequentially:
15	1. `deploy:api` — `wrangler deploy` (Worker to `api.nasapicture.com` + `get.nasapicture.com`)
16	2. `deploy:landing` — `vite build` + `wrangler pages deploy landing/dist/ --project-name nasapicture-landing`
17	
18	## Implementation Plan
19	
20	### 1. Create `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
21	
22	**Trigger**: `push` to `main` (covers PR merges and direct pushes)
23	
24	**Jobs**: Single job with these steps:
25	1. Checkout repo
26	2. Set up Node.js (LTS, e.g. 22.x) — add `.nvmrc` to pin version
27	3. `npm ci` (root deps: wrangler, typescript, workers-types)
28	4. `npm ci --prefix landing` (landing deps: vite, sass)
29	5. `npx tsc --noEmit` — type-check gate, fail the deploy if types are broken
30	6. `npm run deploy` — deploys both Worker and Pages
31	
32	### 2. GitHub Repository Secrets Required
33	
34	| Secret | Purpose |
35	|---|---|
36	| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Wrangler auth for both Worker and Pages deploys |
37	| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | Target Cloudflare account |
38	
39	The API token needs permissions: **Workers Scripts: Edit**, **Cloudflare Pages: Edit**, and **Account Settings: Read**.
40	
41	`NASA_API_KEY` is already set via `wrangler secret` on the Worker itself, so it does not need to be in GitHub secrets.
42	
43	### 3. Add `.nvmrc`
44	
45	Pin Node.js version (e.g. `22`) at the repo root so the workflow and local dev stay in sync.
46	
47	## Workflow Skeleton
48	
49	```yaml
50	name: Deploy
51	on:
52	  push:
53	    branches: [main]
54	
55	jobs:
56	  deploy:
57	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
58	    steps:
59	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
60	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
61	        with:
62	          node-version-file: .nvmrc
63	          cache: npm
64	      - run: npm ci
65	      - run: npm ci --prefix landing
66	      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
67	      - run: npm run deploy
68	        env:
69	          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
70	          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
71	```
72	
73	## Considerations
74	
75	- **Single job vs. split jobs**: A single job is simpler and the total deploy is fast (type-check + wrangler deploy + pages deploy). No need to parallelize until it becomes slow.
76	- **No deploy on non-main branches**: Dev/feature branches never trigger deploys, matching the existing "deploy from main only" rule.
77	- **Failure notifications**: GitHub sends email on workflow failure by default, which is sufficient. Slack/webhook notifications can be added later if needed.
78	- **Caching**: `actions/setup-node` with `cache: npm` caches `~/.npm` across runs, speeding up installs.
79	- **Pages deploy**: `wrangler pages deploy` uses the same `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, no separate Pages token needed.
80
```
</details></tool-use>

7	# Local timezone APOD rollover
8	
9	Users might find it useful (both in the API and the landing page) to choose to get the new image at midnight in their local timezone, instead of when it actually rolls over in ET.
10	
11	## The problem
12	
13	APOD publishes once per day, keyed to Eastern Time. A user in Tokyo (UTC+9) sees the image roll over at 1pm JST -- awkward if they want "a new picture every morning." Conversely, a user in PST sees it change at 9pm, which might actually be fine.
14	
15	## Possible API surface
16	
17	A query parameter like `?tz=Asia/Tokyo` or `?tz=UTC%2B9` on any image endpoint. The Worker would compute "today" in the requested timezone instead of ET, and request that date's APOD.
18	
19	## Key constraint
20	
21	If a user's local date is ahead of ET (e.g., it's April 2 in Tokyo but still April 1 in ET), the April 2 APOD doesn't exist yet. The Worker would need to fall back to the most recent available date, which is what `findLatestImage` already does via lookback. So this might mostly work out of the box -- the timezone param just changes which date the lookback starts from.
22	
23	## Landing page
24	
25	Could detect timezone via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` and pass it to the API. Or let users toggle between "NASA time" and "local time" if we want to keep it explicit.
26	
27	## Phasing
28	
29	Nice-to-have, not critical. Phase 1 could just handle timezones behind ET (west of Eastern), which is straightforward -- the requested date always exists. Timezones ahead of ET (where the date might not exist yet) can come later if there's demand.
30	
31	## Related
32	
33	Ties naturally into TASK-0011 (R2 storage layer for image archiving). If we're storing the last N images anyway, serving a timezone-shifted "yesterday" from the archive is trivial. Any tasks spawned from this note are likely blocked by TASK-0011.
34	
35	## Open questions
36	
37	- Caching implications: timezone-varied requests would reduce cache hit rates since each timezone produces a different date key during the rollover window
38
```

```text
1	---
2	type: note
3	status: inbox
4	created: 2026-04-06
5	---
6	
7	# Serve OG HTML to social crawlers on api.nasapicture.com
8	
9	## Problem
10	
11	Twitter/Facebook/etc. link previews need an HTML page with Open Graph meta tags. When their crawlers hit `api.nasapicture.com/`, the Worker responds with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` (the raw APOD image), so there's no HTML to parse and no card renders. This means tweets linking `api.nasapicture.com` show no preview image.
12	
13	## Fix
14	
15	In the Worker, sniff the `User-Agent` header on incoming requests to the image routes. If the UA matches a known social crawler, return an HTML document with OG tags instead of the image bytes. Otherwise, behave as today and return the image.
16	
17	## Affected routes
18	
19	The crawler check should run before the image response for these route groups in `src/index.ts`:
20	
21	- `hdPaths`: `/`, `/image.jpg`
22	- `sdPaths`: `/sd`, `/image-sd.jpg`
23	- `optimizedPaths`: `/optimized`, `/image-optimized.jpg`
24	- `thumbPaths`: `/thumb`, `/thumb.jpg`
25	
26	The `/info` and `/about` routes already return text, so they don't need this.
27	
28	## Implementation approach
29	
30	1. **Add a `isSocialCrawler(request)` helper** that reads `User-Agent` and tests against a regex of known crawler substrings (case-insensitive).
31	
32	2. **Add a `buildOgHtml(apod, requestUrl)` helper** that takes the APOD metadata (already fetched by `findLatestImage`) and the request URL, and returns a minimal HTML string with OG tags.
33	
34	3. **Insert the check early in each image route block**, after `findLatestImage` resolves but before fetching the upstream image. If it's a crawler, return the OG HTML and skip the image fetch entirely (saves bandwidth and latency).
35	
36	```
37	if (isSocialCrawler(request)) {
38	  const apod = await findLatestImage(log, apiKey);
39	  res = new Response(buildOgHtml(apod, reqUrl), {
40	    headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" }),
41	  });
42	}
43	```
44	
45	Since `findLatestImage` is already called for these routes, the crawler path just skips the image fetch/transform step.
46	
47	## Crawler User-Agents to match (case-insensitive substring)
48	
49	- `Twitterbot`
50	- `facebookexternalhit`
51	- `Facebot`
52	- `Slackbot`
53	- `Discordbot`
54	- `LinkedInBot`
55	- `TelegramBot`
56	- `WhatsApp`
57	- `Pinterest`
58	- `redditbot`
59	
60	## HTML response shape
61	
62	Minimal document with:
63	
64	- `<title>` — APOD title + "| nasapicture.com"
65	- `<meta name="description">` — truncated APOD explanation
66	- `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type=website`, `og:url`
67	- `og:image` — `https://api.nasapicture.com/sd` (standard res is more reliable for card dimensions)
68	- `og:image:width` / `og:image:height` — from `fetchImageDimensions` if available, omit if not
69	- `og:site_name` — "nasapicture.com"
70	- `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`
71	
72	## Caching consideration
73	
74	Crawler responses can use the same cache TTL as regular image responses. The OG HTML is date-keyed (same APOD metadata), so it rolls over at midnight ET like everything else. Consider using a distinct cache key suffix (e.g., `:og`) to avoid serving HTML from the image cache or vice versa.
75	
76	## Testing
77	
78	- Use `curl -A "Twitterbot/1.0"` to verify the crawler path returns HTML
79	- Use `curl` with no special UA to verify normal image behavior is unchanged
80	- Validate the returned HTML with the [Twitter Card Validator](https://cards-dev.twitter.com/validator) and [Facebook Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/)
81
```

8	# Add a user-facing gallery of past APOD images
9	
10	A browsable archive/gallery showing past Astronomy Pictures of the Day. Depends on TASK-0011 (R2 storage layer) being in place to persist historical images.
11	
12	## Why
13	
14	The daily APOD is ephemeral by design, but visitors naturally want to browse past images. A gallery turns the site from a single-serving utility into something worth revisiting. NASA's own APOD archive is functional but not visually engaging, so there's room to offer a better browsing experience that matches the project's aesthetic.
15	
16	## Data available from R2
17	
18	TASK-0011 defines the R2 key structure as:
19	
20	- `{date}/hd.{ext}` — HD image
21	- `{date}/sd.{ext}` — SD image
22	- `{date}/info.json` — metadata snapshot (title, explanation, copyright, dimensions)
23	
24	The `info.json` sidecar gives us everything we need for gallery cards without hitting NASA's API. The archive builds organically from the day R2 goes live, one image per day.
25	
26	## API surface
27	
28	The gallery needs a way to list and fetch archived images. Options:
29	
30	- **New route: `/archive`** — returns JSON listing of available dates (from R2 `list()`)
31	- **New route: `/archive/{date}`** — returns image for a specific date (from R2)
32	- **New route: `/archive/{date}/info`** — returns metadata for a specific date
33	
34	Alternatively, the existing `/info?date=2026-04-01` could accept a date param. But dedicated archive routes are cleaner and avoid overloading the "today" endpoints.
35	
36	## Frontend
37	
38	### Location
39	Could live on the landing page as a section below the hero, or as a dedicated `/gallery` page. A separate page avoids bloating the clean single-page landing, and gives room for richer browsing UX.
40	
41	### Layout ideas
42	- Thumbnail grid using Cloudflare Image Transformations (same approach as `/thumb` route, but per-date)
43	- Click/tap to expand with title, explanation, and full-res image
44	- Date-based navigation (calendar picker or month groupings)
45	- Infinite scroll or paginated grid

47	### Performance
48	- Grid thumbnails via `cf.image` transforms (small, blurred placeholders with lazy-loaded sharper versions)
49	- Pre-sized containers using dimensions from `info.json` (same pattern as the current hero image)
50	- Paginate R2 `list()` calls to avoid loading the entire archive at once

54	- **TASK-0011** (blocker): R2 storage layer that archives images and metadata daily
55	- **EPIC-0002**: Landing page polish, gallery would be a major addition under this umbrella

58	- **NOTE-0016**: Local timezone rollover also depends on R2 and date-keyed image access

64	- Search/filter by title or keyword, or just date-based browsing?
65	- Should the gallery be part of the Cloudflare Pages landing site, or served by the Worker?

# Add R2 storage layer for APOD image archiving

Add Cloudflare R2 as a persistent storage/origin layer between edge cache and NASA API. Every image fetched from NASA gets stored in R2, building an automatic archive and providing resilience if NASA is slow or down.

## Infrastructure

- Create R2 bucket (e.g., `apod-archive`)
- Add R2 binding in `wrangler.toml`: `[[r2_buckets]]` with `binding = "APOD_ARCHIVE"`
- Update `Env` interface in `src/index.ts` to include the R2 binding

## R2 key structure

- `{date}/hd.{ext}` — HD image
- `{date}/sd.{ext}` — SD image
- `{date}/info.json` — metadata snapshot

# Serve video APOD thumbnail instead of walking back

## Problem

When today's APOD is a video, the service walks back up to 7 days to find an image. This means the image endpoints can show content that's days old and doesn't match the `/info` metadata.

## Approach

NASA's APOD API sometimes includes a `thumbnail_url` field for video entries. If present, serve that as the image instead of walking back.

1. Add `thumbnail_url?: string` to the `ApodResponse` type
2. In `findLatestImage` (or a new function), check today's APOD first: if `media_type === "video"` and `thumbnail_url` exists, return that entry with the thumbnail URL mapped to the `url`/`hdurl` fields
3. If no thumbnail is available, fall back to the existing walkback logic
4. Update `/info` to indicate when the image is a video thumbnail (e.g. `"source": "video_thumbnail"`)

# HTML scraping fallback for NASA API outages

## Problem

NASA's API can return 500 while the actual APOD webpage (`apod.nasa.gov/apod/`) serves normally. Once the 24h stale cache expires with no traffic to refresh it, the Worker has nothing to serve. This happened on 2026-04-08.

## Implementation

1. Add a `scrapeApodPage(log, date?)` function that fetches `https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/` (or `apYYMMDD.html` for specific dates)
2. Use regex extraction (no DOM parser in Workers) to pull: image URL (HD + SD), title, date, explanation, copyright, media type (img vs iframe)
3. Image URLs from the page are relative paths, prefix with `https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/`
4. Insert the call in `fetchApodFromNasa` after stale cache miss, before throwing `NasaApiError`
5. Populate both primary (6h) and stale (24h) caches with the scraped result
6. Log clearly when scrape fallback activates

## Considerations

- Regex parsing is fragile but the APOD page layout hasn't changed in years

# Automated daily cache warming via Cron Trigger

## Problem

The Worker relies on visitor traffic to populate edge cache. With low traffic, the first visitor after APOD rollover gets a slow uncached response. Worse, if NASA's API is down and stale cache has expired, there's nothing to serve at all.

## Implementation

1. Add a `[triggers]` block to `wrangler.toml` with a cron schedule (e.g., `30 5 * * *` for 00:30 ET)
2. Export a `scheduled()` handler alongside the existing `fetch()` handler
3. The handler calls `findLatestImage`, `fetchImageCached` (HD + SD), and `fetchImageDimensions` to populate both cache tiers
4. Consider a second cron run (e.g., every 6h) to keep caches warm within the 6h primary TTL

## Considerations

- NASA sometimes publishes late after midnight ET; 00:30 ET is a reasonable first attempt
- Cron Triggers run in a single colo, so only that edge gets warmed. Other regions still cold on first hit, but API metadata is cached and NASA image fetches are fast.
- A single daily run doesn't cover the full 6h primary TTL. Running every 4-6h or accepting off-peak cold caches are both viable.

# Annotated image endpoint with title and explanation

## Idea

A new endpoint (e.g., `/annotated` or `/card`) that composites the APOD title and explanation onto the image. Useful as a wallpaper with built-in caption, a shareable card, or a daily briefing image.

## Open questions

- **Rendering approach**: Workers have no canvas/DOM. Options: SVG foreignObject via CF image transforms, Satori/resvg-wasm bundled in the Worker, or pre-rendered via R2 + external job.
- **Text length**: Full explanation can be paragraphs. Truncation or summary needed.
- **Layout**: Text overlay on image (readability risk) vs. extended canvas with text panel.
- **Shared infra with NOTE-0008** (OG image): both composite text on images, could share a rendering pipeline.

## Related

- NOTE-0008 (OG image generation)
- NOTE-0024 (original exploration)

Add a short content block between the hero image and the endpoint docs that explains what APOD is and what nasapicture.com solves. Spawned from NOTE-0006.

## What to cover

- **What is APOD?** NASA has published a new Astronomy Picture of the Day every day since 1995, each with a professional explanation from astronomers.

- Reads naturally to a non-technical visitor

# Auto-refresh landing page on APOD rollover

When a user leaves the landing page open, the image and caption should update automatically when NASA publishes the new APOD. Spawned from NOTE-0010.

## Approach

Two phases: a coarse countdown that converges on midnight ET, then burst polling to catch the exact publish moment.

### Phase 1: countdown

- On page load, store `currentDate` from initial `/info` response
- Compute clock offset from that response's `Date` header: `serverTime - localTime`
- `setInterval` every 5 minutes recalculates ms until midnight ET using the offset. Self-corrects for timer drift and background-tab throttling.

### Phase 2: burst polling

- When under 5 minutes remain, clear the interval and poll `/info` every 2 minutes
- When `data.date !== currentDate`, call `updateApod(data)`, stop polling, re-enter phase 1
- Cap burst at 30 minutes (15 requests max); if no change, re-enter phase 1

### Visibility handler

- On `visibilitychange` to visible, do an immediate `/info` check to catch long-hidden tabs

## Image transition on rollover

- Fade out current image (remove `.loaded`), fetch new `/thumb`, set as wrapper background
- Cache-bust: `img.src = ${API_BASE}/optimized?d=${data.date}` and `?d=` on the thumb fetch too
- Update aspect ratio from new dimensions; fade back in on `img.load`
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (skip fade, show immediately)
- Revoke previous blob URL with `URL.revokeObjectURL()` to avoid leaks

## Implementation notes

- Refactor initial caption/image/thumbnail setup into a reusable `updateApod(data)` function
- All changes in `landing/index.html` script block, no Worker changes
- Cache keys roll at midnight ET so post-midnight `/info` requests cache-miss and fetch fresh from NASA
- Zero new dependencies

## Acceptance

- Tab open across midnight ET updates image and caption with a fade transition
- `visibilitychange` triggers an immediate check after long-hidden state
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`
- No memory leak from blob URLs across rollovers

```

# Fix focus toggle markup and discoverability

The focus toggle now has visible "Focus" text alongside the icon, but the markup was not updated when the label was added. Spawned from NOTE-0017 (remaining items).

## Problems

- **Accessible-name mismatch.** `index.html:131` has `aria-label="Dim the lights"` but the visible `<span class="label">` says "Focus". When a button has visible text, `aria-label` overrides what screen readers announce, so sighted users see "Focus" while screen reader users hear "Dim the lights". WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) failure.
- **No toggle semantics.** This is a binary on/off toggle but has no `aria-pressed` state. Assistive tech can't tell whether focus mode is active.
- **Redundant `title` tooltip.** Now that text is visible, the `title="Dim the lights"` attribute is noise (and also stale).
- **Tiny label size.** `.label` is `font-size: 0.5rem` (~8px) at `_focus-mode.scss:29`, smaller than ideal for discoverability.

## Fix

- Remove `aria-label` (let the visible "Focus" text be the accessible name), or update it to match the visible text
- Remove the `title` attribute
- Add `aria-pressed` reflecting focus-mode state, updated in the click handler when `.focus-mode` is toggled on `body`
- Bump `.label` font-size so it reads clearly without squinting (tune alongside icon for balance)

## Acceptance

- Accessible name matches visible text (no mismatch flagged by axe / Lighthouse)
- `aria-pressed="true"` when focus mode is active, `"false"` otherwise
- Label is readable at default zoom without squinting
- Existing focus-mode behavior (overlay, Esc, overlay click to exit) is unchanged

# Local timezone APOD rollover

Let users receive the new image at midnight in their local timezone instead of waiting for ET rollover. Spawned from NOTE-0016. Nice-to-have, blocked by TASK-0011 (R2 archive) because ahead-of-ET timezones need an archived "yesterday" image to serve.

## The problem

APOD publishes once per day keyed to Eastern Time. A user in Tokyo sees the image roll over at 1pm JST, which is awkward if they want "a new picture every morning." A user in PST sees it at 9pm, which may be acceptable.

## API surface

Query param on image and `/info` routes, e.g. `?tz=Asia/Tokyo`. Worker computes "today" in that timezone and requests that date's APOD.

- **West of ET** (the requested date always exists): lookback handles anything missing, works today without R2.
- **Ahead of ET** (e.g., Asia/Pacific, requested date may not exist yet): serve the most recent archived image from R2.

## Landing page

Detect timezone via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` and pass it to the API. Consider an explicit "NASA time / local time" toggle so the behavior is never hidden from users.

## Phasing

1. **Phase 1** — west-of-ET only, ships without R2. Covers the common US case.
2. **Phase 2** — ahead-of-ET, requires TASK-0011 to serve the previous day when the new one doesn't exist yet.

## Open questions

- Timezone-varied requests reduce cache hit rate during the rollover window. Measure impact, consider bucketing `tz` params into ET offset groups if it matters.

## Acceptance

- `?tz=` respected on image and `/info` routes
- Landing page rollover respects local timezone when available
- Phase 1 works for west-of-ET without R2
- Documented in `/about`

# GitHub Action auto-deploy on merge to main

Automate the manual `npm run deploy` step after each PR merge so Worker and Pages both deploy on `push` to `main`. Spawned from NOTE-0014.

## Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:

\```yaml
name: Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm ci --prefix landing
      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
      - run: npm run deploy
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
\```

## Prerequisites

- Add `.nvmrc` at the repo root pinning Node LTS (e.g., `22`) so CI and local dev stay in sync
- GitHub repository secrets:
  - `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` — needs **Workers Scripts: Edit**, **Cloudflare Pages: Edit**, **Account Settings: Read**
  - `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` — target account
- `NASA_API_KEY` is already set via `wrangler secret` on the Worker, no GH secret needed

## Considerations

- Single job is sufficient; total deploy is fast enough not to need parallelization
- Type-check is a gate so a broken build never deploys
- `actions/setup-node` with `cache: npm` speeds up repeat installs
- Only triggers on `main`, matching the "deploy from main only" rule
- GitHub's default email-on-failure notification is sufficient; Slack webhook can be added later

## Acceptance

- PR merge to `main` triggers the workflow
- Type-check failure blocks the deploy
- Worker and Pages both deploy from one job
- Manual `npm run deploy` after merges is no longer needed

# Generate daily OG image (1200x630) with workers-og

Render a new Open Graph image daily with the APOD photo cropped to 1200x630 and branded with a nasapicture.com wordmark. Spawned from NOTE-0008.

## Why

The current `og:image` points to `https://api.nasapicture.com/image.jpg`, which serves the raw APOD at whatever dimensions NASA provides (often square or portrait). Social platforms expect 1200x630 for optimal link previews.

## Approach: workers-og

[`workers-og`](https://github.com/kvnang/workers-og) renders HTML/CSS to PNG inside the Worker via Satori. No browser, no external service, free Workers tier.

### Implementation

1. Add a `/og` route to `src/index.ts`
2. Handler calls `findLatestImage` to get today's metadata, then renders an HTML template with the APOD image as background, title text, and nasapicture.com wordmark
3. Cache the PNG aggressively (24h TTL keyed to date) — one cold generation per day
4. Update the `og:image` meta tag in `landing/index.html` to point to `https://api.nasapicture.com/og`
5. Embed fonts (Source Serif / Sans) as ArrayBuffer imports

### Constraints (from NOTE-0008)

- Satori supports flexbox only (no grid)
- Custom fonts must be embedded as ArrayBuffers, adds to Worker bundle size
- Only a subset of CSS is supported — keep the template minimal

## Alternative (fallback if quality isn't sufficient)

Cloudflare Images binding (`env.IMAGES`) to resize/crop the APOD natively, then `.draw()` a pre-rendered text overlay PNG on top. Higher-fidelity resizing with smart crop/gravity. Free tier is 5,000 transformations/month; we'd use ~30. More moving parts, don't reach for it unless workers-og isn't good enough.

## Related

- TASK-0034 (OG HTML for crawlers) — benefits from this being in place
- TASK-0022 (annotated image endpoint) — shares the rendering pipeline, candidate for refactor after both land

## Acceptance

- `GET /og` returns a valid 1200x630 PNG
- Response cached for 24h, regenerates on rollover
- Twitter Card Validator and Facebook Sharing Debugger render the new image correctly
- Worker bundle size stays reasonable (measure before/after)

```

# Serve OG HTML to social crawlers on api.nasapicture.com

When Twitter/Facebook/Slack/etc. crawl `api.nasapicture.com/`, the Worker responds with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` and no HTML, so link previews fail to render. Sniff the User-Agent and return an HTML document with OG tags for known crawlers, unchanged image bytes for everyone else. Spawned from NOTE-0020.

## Affected routes

Add the crawler check early in each image route block in `src/index.ts`, after `findLatestImage` resolves but before fetching upstream bytes:

- `hdPaths`: `/`, `/image.jpg`
- `sdPaths`: `/sd`, `/image-sd.jpg`
- `optimizedPaths`: `/optimized`, `/image-optimized.jpg`
- `thumbPaths`: `/thumb`, `/thumb.jpg`

`/info` and `/about` already return text; they don't need this.

## Implementation

1. `isSocialCrawler(request)` helper that tests the `User-Agent` header against a case-insensitive substring list
2. `buildOgHtml(apod, requestUrl)` helper that returns a minimal HTML document with OG + Twitter-card tags
3. Insert early in each image route, skipping the image fetch entirely on the crawler path:

\```ts
if (isSocialCrawler(request)) {
  const apod = await findLatestImage(log, apiKey);
  res = new Response(buildOgHtml(apod, reqUrl), {
    headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" }),
  });
}
\```

## Crawler substrings (case-insensitive)

`Twitterbot`, `facebookexternalhit`, `Facebot`, `Slackbot`, `Discordbot`, `LinkedInBot`, `TelegramBot`, `WhatsApp`, `Pinterest`, `redditbot`

## HTML shape

- `<title>`: APOD title + " | nasapicture.com"
- `<meta name="description">`: truncated APOD explanation
- `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type=website`, `og:url`
- `og:image`: `https://api.nasapicture.com/og` once TASK-0033 ships, otherwise `/sd` (SD is more reliable for card dimensions than HD)
- `og:image:width` / `og:image:height` from `fetchImageDimensions` when available; omit if not
- `og:site_name`: `nasapicture.com`
- `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`

## Caching

Distinct cache key suffix (e.g. `:og`) so HTML and image caches don't collide. Same 6h primary / 24h stale TTL as the image responses.

## Testing

- `curl -A "Twitterbot/1.0" https://api.nasapicture.com/` returns HTML with OG tags
- `curl https://api.nasapicture.com/` (default UA) still returns image bytes
- Validate with Twitter Card Validator and Facebook Sharing Debugger

## Acceptance

- All listed crawlers receive HTML with OG/Twitter tags on image routes
- Non-crawler requests are unchanged
- No regression in image response caching

7	# Social Sharing Previews
8	
9	Make link previews render correctly on Twitter, Slack, Facebook, Discord, iMessage, and friends. Covers both the HTML surface (so crawlers see OG tags instead of image bytes) and the image asset itself (so the preview is sized and cropped for social platforms).

18	
19	Render a 1200x630 branded PNG once per day inside the Worker via Satori. Cached 24h keyed to date, regenerates at rollover. The OG HTML then points `og:image` at `/og` instead of `/sd`.
20	
21	## Sequence
22	
23	1. **TASK-0034 first** (OG HTML) — immediately fixes preview rendering even using the raw image URL for `og:image`

1	---
2	type: task
3	status: backlog
4	priority: 2
5	created: 2026-04-09
6	parent: EPIC-0002
7	---
8	
9	# Auto-refresh landing page on APOD rollover
10	
11	When a user leaves the landing page open, the image and caption should update automatically when NASA publishes the new APOD. Spawned from NOTE-0010.
12	
13	## Approach
14	
15	Two phases: a coarse countdown that converges on midnight ET, then burst polling to catch the exact publish moment.
16	
17	### Phase 1: countdown
18	
19	- On page load, store `currentDate` from initial `/info` response
20	- Compute clock offset from that response's `Date` header: `serverTime - localTime`
21	- `setInterval` every 5 minutes recalculates ms until midnight ET using the offset. Self-corrects for timer drift and background-tab throttling.
22	
23	### Phase 2: burst polling
24	
25	- When under 5 minutes remain, clear the interval and poll `/info` every 2 minutes
26	- When `data.date !== currentDate`, call `updateApod(data)`, stop polling, re-enter phase 1
27	- Cap burst at 30 minutes (15 requests max); if no change, re-enter phase 1
28	
29	### Visibility handler
30	
31	- On `visibilitychange` to visible, do an immediate `/info` check to catch long-hidden tabs
32	
33	## Image transition on rollover
34	
35	- Fade out current image (remove `.loaded`), fetch new `/thumb`, set as wrapper background
36	- Cache-bust: `img.src = ${API_BASE}/optimized?d=${data.date}` and `?d=` on the thumb fetch too
37	- Update aspect ratio from new dimensions; fade back in on `img.load`
38	- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (skip fade, show immediately)
39	- Revoke previous blob URL with `URL.revokeObjectURL()` to avoid leaks
40	
41	## Implementation notes
42	
43	- Refactor initial caption/image/thumbnail setup into a reusable `updateApod(data)` function
44	- All changes in `landing/index.html` script block, no Worker changes
45	- Cache keys roll at midnight ET so post-midnight `/info` requests cache-miss and fetch fresh from NASA
46	- Zero new dependencies
47	
48	## Acceptance
49	
50	- Tab open across midnight ET updates image and caption with a fade transition
51	- `visibilitychange` triggers an immediate check after long-hidden state
52	- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`
53	- No memory leak from blob URLs across rollovers
54
```
</details></tool-use>

8	
9	# Fix focus toggle markup and discoverability
10	
11	The focus toggle now has visible "Focus" text alongside the icon, but the markup was not updated when the label was added. Spawned from NOTE-0017 (remaining items).
12	
13	## Problems
14	
15	- **Accessible-name mismatch.** `index.html:131` has `aria-label="Dim the lights"` but the visible `<span class="label">` says "Focus". When a button has visible text, `aria-label` overrides what screen readers announce, so sighted users see "Focus" while screen reader users hear "Dim the lights". WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) failure.
16	- **No toggle semantics.** This is a binary on/off toggle but has no `aria-pressed` state. Assistive tech can't tell whether focus mode is active.
17	- **Redundant `title` tooltip.** Now that text is visible, the `title="Dim the lights"` attribute is noise (and also stale).
18	- **Tiny label size.** `.label` is `font-size: 0.5rem` (~8px) at `_focus-mode.scss:29`, smaller than ideal for discoverability.
19	
20	## Fix
21	
22	- Remove `aria-label` (let the visible "Focus" text be the accessible name), or update it to match the visible text
23	- Remove the `title` attribute
24	- Add `aria-pressed` reflecting focus-mode state, updated in the click handler when `.focus-mode` is toggled on `body`
25	- Bump `.label` font-size so it reads clearly without squinting (tune alongside icon for balance)
26	
27	## Acceptance
28	
29	- Accessible name matches visible text (no mismatch flagged by axe / Lighthouse)
30	- `aria-pressed="true"` when focus mode is active, `"false"` otherwise
31	- Label is readable at default zoom without squinting
32	- Existing focus-mode behavior (overlay, Esc, overlay click to exit) is unchanged
33

1	---

9	
10	# Local timezone APOD rollover
11	
12	Let users receive the new image at midnight in their local timezone instead of waiting for ET rollover. Spawned from NOTE-0016. Nice-to-have, blocked by TASK-0011 (R2 archive) because ahead-of-ET timezones need an archived "yesterday" image to serve.
13	
14	## The problem
15	
16	APOD publishes once per day keyed to Eastern Time. A user in Tokyo sees the image roll over at 1pm JST, which is awkward if they want "a new picture every morning." A user in PST sees it at 9pm, which may be acceptable.
17	
18	## API surface
19	
20	Query param on image and `/info` routes, e.g. `?tz=Asia/Tokyo`. Worker computes "today" in that timezone and requests that date's APOD.
21	
22	- **West of ET** (the requested date always exists): lookback handles anything missing, works today without R2.
23	- **Ahead of ET** (e.g., Asia/Pacific, requested date may not exist yet): serve the most recent archived image from R2.
24	
25	## Landing page
26	
27	Detect timezone via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` and pass it to the API. Consider an explicit "NASA time / local time" toggle so the behavior is never hidden from users.
28	
29	## Phasing
30	
31	1. **Phase 1** — west-of-ET only, ships without R2. Covers the common US case.
32	2. **Phase 2** — ahead-of-ET, requires TASK-0011 to serve the previous day when the new one doesn't exist yet.
33	
34	## Open questions
35	
36	- Timezone-varied requests reduce cache hit rate during the rollover window. Measure impact, consider bucketing `tz` params into ET offset groups if it matters.
37	
38	## Acceptance
39	
40	- `?tz=` respected on image and `/info` routes
41	- Landing page rollover respects local timezone when available
42	- Phase 1 works for west-of-ET without R2
43	- Documented in `/about`
44
```
</details></tool-use>

1	---

7	---
8	
9	# GitHub Action auto-deploy on merge to main
10	
11	Automate the manual `npm run deploy` step after each PR merge so Worker and Pages both deploy on `push` to `main`. Spawned from NOTE-0014.
12	
13	## Workflow
14	
15	Create `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:
16	
17	```yaml
18	name: Deploy
19	on:
20	  push:
21	    branches: [main]
22	
23	jobs:
24	  deploy:
25	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
26	    steps:
27	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
28	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
29	        with:
30	          node-version-file: .nvmrc
31	          cache: npm
32	      - run: npm ci
33	      - run: npm ci --prefix landing
34	      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
35	      - run: npm run deploy
36	        env:
37	          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
38	          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
39	```
40	
41	## Prerequisites
42	
43	- Add `.nvmrc` at the repo root pinning Node LTS (e.g., `22`) so CI and local dev stay in sync
44	- GitHub repository secrets:
45	  - `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` — needs **Workers Scripts: Edit**, **Cloudflare Pages: Edit**, **Account Settings: Read**
46	  - `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` — target account
47	- `NASA_API_KEY` is already set via `wrangler secret` on the Worker, no GH secret needed
48	
49	## Considerations
50	
51	- Single job is sufficient; total deploy is fast enough not to need parallelization
52	- Type-check is a gate so a broken build never deploys
53	- `actions/setup-node` with `cache: npm` speeds up repeat installs
54	- Only triggers on `main`, matching the "deploy from main only" rule
55	- GitHub's default email-on-failure notification is sufficient; Slack webhook can be added later
56	
57	## Acceptance
58	
59	- PR merge to `main` triggers the workflow
60	- Type-check failure blocks the deploy
61	- Worker and Pages both deploy from one job
62	- Manual `npm run deploy` after merges is no longer needed
63
```
</details></tool-use>

8	
9	# Generate daily OG image (1200x630) with workers-og
10	
11	Render a new Open Graph image daily with the APOD photo cropped to 1200x630 and branded with a nasapicture.com wordmark. Spawned from NOTE-0008.
12	
13	## Why
14	
15	The current `og:image` points to `https://api.nasapicture.com/image.jpg`, which serves the raw APOD at whatever dimensions NASA provides (often square or portrait). Social platforms expect 1200x630 for optimal link previews.
16	
17	## Approach: workers-og
18	
19	[`workers-og`](https://github.com/kvnang/workers-og) renders HTML/CSS to PNG inside the Worker via Satori. No browser, no external service, free Workers tier.
20	
21	### Implementation
22	
23	1. Add a `/og` route to `src/index.ts`
24	2. Handler calls `findLatestImage` to get today's metadata, then renders an HTML template with the APOD image as background, title text, and nasapicture.com wordmark
25	3. Cache the PNG aggressively (24h TTL keyed to date) — one cold generation per day
26	4. Update the `og:image` meta tag in `landing/index.html` to point to `https://api.nasapicture.com/og`
27	5. Embed fonts (Source Serif / Sans) as ArrayBuffer imports
28	
29	### Constraints (from NOTE-0008)
30	
31	- Satori supports flexbox only (no grid)
32	- Custom fonts must be embedded as ArrayBuffers, adds to Worker bundle size
33	- Only a subset of CSS is supported — keep the template minimal
34	
35	## Alternative (fallback if quality isn't sufficient)
36	
37	Cloudflare Images binding (`env.IMAGES`) to resize/crop the APOD natively, then `.draw()` a pre-rendered text overlay PNG on top. Higher-fidelity resizing with smart crop/gravity. Free tier is 5,000 transformations/month; we'd use ~30. More moving parts, don't reach for it unless workers-og isn't good enough.
38	
39	## Related
40	
41	- TASK-0034 (OG HTML for crawlers) — benefits from this being in place
42	- TASK-0022 (annotated image endpoint) — shares the rendering pipeline, candidate for refactor after both land
43	
44	## Acceptance
45	
46	- `GET /og` returns a valid 1200x630 PNG
47	- Response cached for 24h, regenerates on rollover
48	- Twitter Card Validator and Facebook Sharing Debugger render the new image correctly
49	- Worker bundle size stays reasonable (measure before/after)
50
```
</details></tool-use>

1	---
2	type: task
3	status: backlog
4	priority: 2
5	created: 2026-04-09
6	parent: EPIC-0005
7	---
8	
9	# Serve OG HTML to social crawlers on api.nasapicture.com
10	
11	When Twitter/Facebook/Slack/etc. crawl `api.nasapicture.com/`, the Worker responds with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` and no HTML, so link previews fail to render. Sniff the User-Agent and return an HTML document with OG tags for known crawlers, unchanged image bytes for everyone else. Spawned from NOTE-0020.
12	
13	## Affected routes
14	
15	Add the crawler check early in each image route block in `src/index.ts`, after `findLatestImage` resolves but before fetching upstream bytes:
16	
17	- `hdPaths`: `/`, `/image.jpg`
18	- `sdPaths`: `/sd`, `/image-sd.jpg`
19	- `optimizedPaths`: `/optimized`, `/image-optimized.jpg`
20	- `thumbPaths`: `/thumb`, `/thumb.jpg`
21	
22	`/info` and `/about` already return text; they don't need this.
23	
24	## Implementation
25	
26	1. `isSocialCrawler(request)` helper that tests the `User-Agent` header against a case-insensitive substring list
27	2. `buildOgHtml(apod, requestUrl)` helper that returns a minimal HTML document with OG + Twitter-card tags
28	3. Insert early in each image route, skipping the image fetch entirely on the crawler path:
29	
30	```ts
31	if (isSocialCrawler(request)) {
32	  const apod = await findLatestImage(log, apiKey);
33	  res = new Response(buildOgHtml(apod, reqUrl), {
34	    headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" }),
35	  });
36	}
37	```
38	
39	## Crawler substrings (case-insensitive)
40	
41	`Twitterbot`, `facebookexternalhit`, `Facebot`, `Slackbot`, `Discordbot`, `LinkedInBot`, `TelegramBot`, `WhatsApp`, `Pinterest`, `redditbot`
42	
43	## HTML shape
44	
45	- `<title>`: APOD title + " | nasapicture.com"
46	- `<meta name="description">`: truncated APOD explanation
47	- `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type=website`, `og:url`
48	- `og:image`: `https://api.nasapicture.com/og` once TASK-0033 ships, otherwise `/sd` (SD is more reliable for card dimensions than HD)
49	- `og:image:width` / `og:image:height` from `fetchImageDimensions` when available; omit if not
50	- `og:site_name`: `nasapicture.com`
51	- `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`
52	
53	## Caching
54	
55	Distinct cache key suffix (e.g. `:og`) so HTML and image caches don't collide. Same 6h primary / 24h stale TTL as the image responses.
56	
57	## Testing
58	
59	- `curl -A "Twitterbot/1.0" https://api.nasapicture.com/` returns HTML with OG tags
60	- `curl https://api.nasapicture.com/` (default UA) still returns image bytes
61	- Validate with Twitter Card Validator and Facebook Sharing Debugger
62	
63	## Acceptance
64	
65	- All listed crawlers receive HTML with OG/Twitter tags on image routes
66	- Non-crawler requests are unchanged
67	- No regression in image response caching
68
```
</details></tool-use>

6	
7	# Infrastructure and DevOps
8	
9	Remove manual steps from the deploy workflow and add durable storage so the service doesn't depend on NASA's uptime for every cache miss.
10	
11	## Tasks
12	
13	### TASK-0011: Add R2 storage layer for APOD image archiving
14	
15	Insert R2 between edge cache and NASA as a persistent origin. Every image fetched from NASA gets stored in R2, building an automatic archive. Layered lookup becomes: Edge cache -> R2 -> NASA.
16	
17	Key structure: `{date}/hd.{ext}`, `{date}/sd.{ext}`, `{date}/info.json`. Current-day images re-validated against NASA for same-day corrections; past dates served from R2 unconditionally.
18	
19	R2 archiving also unblocks NOTE-0016 (local timezone rollover), since serving a timezone-shifted "yesterday" from the archive is trivial.
20	
21	Blocked by TASK-0010.
22	
23	### TASK-0020: HTML scraping fallback for NASA API outages
24	
25	When the NASA API returns non-200 and stale cache is empty, scrape the APOD webpage (`apod.nasa.gov/apod/`) as a last-resort data source. Regex extraction, populates both cache tiers. Only fires when all other sources are exhausted.
26	
27	### TASK-0021: Automated daily cache warming via Cron Trigger
28	
29	Add a `scheduled()` handler with a cron trigger to warm the edge cache after APOD rollover. Calls `findLatestImage`, `fetchImageCached`, and `fetchImageDimensions` to populate metadata and image bytes proactively.
30	
31	### TASK-0032: GitHub Action auto-deploy on merge to main
32	
33	Workflow triggered on push to `main`. Runs type-check (`npx tsc --noEmit`) as a gate, then `npm run deploy`. Requires `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` as repository secrets. Spawned from NOTE-0014.
34	
35	## Sequence
36	
37	1. R2 storage layer (TASK-0011) -- larger effort, independent of deploy automation
38	2. HTML scraping fallback (TASK-0020) -- resilience, no dependencies
39	3. Cron cache warming (TASK-0021) -- resilience, benefits from TASK-0020 being in place
40	4. GitHub Action (TASK-0032) -- small, can be done anytime
41	
42	## Cross-EPIC Dependencies
43	
44	- EPIC-0002 NOTE-0016 (local timezone rollover) is blocked by TASK-0011 (R2 archiving)
45
```

8	
9	# Auto-refresh landing page on APOD rollover
10	
11	If a user leaves the landing page open, the image and caption should update automatically when NASA publishes the new APOD — no manual reload required.
12	
13	## Approach: Self-correcting countdown + short-burst polling
14	
15	Two phases: a coarse countdown that converges on midnight ET, then burst polling to catch the exact publish moment.
16	
17	### Phase 1: Countdown
18	
19	On page load, compute the offset between the user's clock and CF server time (from the `/info` response `Date` header). Use this offset to calculate a corrected "time until midnight ET." Run a `setInterval` every 5 minutes that recalculates the remaining time. This self-corrects for:
20	- Long `setTimeout` drift (browsers throttle timers in background tabs)
21	- Tabs hidden for hours or days (each tick recalculates from scratch)
22	- No single long timeout that fires late or not at all
23	
24	When the countdown shows <5 minutes to midnight ET, transition to phase 2.
25	
26	### Phase 2: Burst polling
27	
28	Poll `/info` every 2 minutes, comparing `data.date` to `currentDate`. When the date changes, call `updateApod(data)` and stop polling. Cap at 30 minutes (15 requests max), then re-enter phase 1 and schedule the next midnight.
29	
30	Total requests per rollover: ~15. Total requests the rest of the day: zero.
31	
32	### Sequence
33	
34	1. On page load, store `currentDate` from initial `/info` response
35	2. Compute clock offset from CF `Date` header: `serverTime - localTime`
36	3. Start 5-min `setInterval` that recalculates ms until midnight ET using the offset
37	4. When <5 min remain, clear the interval and start 2-min burst polling
38	5. When `data.date !== currentDate`, call `updateApod(data)`, stop polling, re-enter step 3 for next day
39	6. After 30 min with no date change, stop polling and re-enter step 3
40	7. On `visibilitychange` to visible, do an immediate `/info` check (catches long-hidden tabs)
41	
42	### Image transition on rollover
43	
44	- Fade out current image (remove `.loaded` class)
45	- Fetch new `/thumb`, set as wrapper background
46	- Cache-bust the image by appending the new date: `img.src = \`${API_BASE}/optimized?d=${data.date}\``
47	- Update aspect ratio from new dimensions
48	- On `img.load`, fade back in
49	- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (skip fade, show immediately)
50	- Swap happens regardless of focus mode
51	
52	### Time source: CF `Date` header (preferred)
53	
54	Use the `Date` response header from the initial `/info` fetch as the authoritative time source. This comes from Cloudflare's edge server (NTP-synced), so it's reliable regardless of the user's local clock. Parse it to compute ms until midnight ET, no extra requests needed.
55	
56	```js
57	const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/info`);
58	const serverNow = new Date(res.headers.get('Date'));
59	// compute ms until midnight ET from serverNow
60	```
61	
62	### Alternatives considered
63	
64	**User's local clock** — Could use `new Date()` from the user's machine to compute time until midnight ET. Simpler, but assumes the user's clock is accurate. Rejected because clock skew on user machines is common enough to cause missed or premature rollovers.
65	
66	**External time APIs** — worldtimeapi.org and timeapi.io are free, no-key options. Unnecessary here since we already get authoritative time from the CF `Date` header, but available if we ever need a dedicated time source.
67	
68	### Edge cases
69	
70	- **Browser image cache** — The `/optimized` URL doesn't change day-to-day, so the browser may serve a stale cached image on rollover. Bust it with a date query param: `/optimized?d=2026-04-05`. The Worker ignores query params for routing but the browser treats it as a new URL.
71	- **Multiple rollovers** — After each successful rollover, re-enter the countdown phase for the next midnight. Not a one-time setup.
72	- **Tab hidden for days** — The `visibilitychange` handler does an immediate `/info` check, catching any missed rollovers regardless of how long the tab was hidden.
73	- **Thumb cache busting** — Same browser cache issue as `/optimized` applies to `/thumb`. Append `?d=${data.date}` to the thumb fetch on rollover too.
74	- **Object URL cleanup** — Each rollover creates a new blob URL for the thumbnail via `URL.createObjectURL()`. Revoke the previous one with `URL.revokeObjectURL()` to avoid memory leaks.
75	
76	### Implementation notes
77	
78	- Refactor initial caption/image/thumbnail setup into a reusable `updateApod(data)` function
79	- All changes in `landing/index.html` script block, no Worker changes needed
80	- Cache keys are date-based and roll at midnight ET, so post-midnight `/info` requests will cache-miss for the new date and fetch fresh from NASA
81	- Zero new dependencies
82
```
</details></tool-use>

18	# Landing page design critique (April 2026)
19	
20	Captured: 2026-04-03 ~9:30 PM CT, dev site at localhost:8788
21	
22	## Anti-Patterns Verdict: Pass
23	
24	No AI slop detected. No purple gradients, glassmorphism, glowing accents, or template layouts. Color palette is disciplined void-black-to-silver monochrome. Typography from Adobe Typekit (Source Serif 4 Display, Source Sans 3, Source Code Pro) is distinctive. Layout trusts the APOD image to carry the page.
25	
26	## Design Health Score: 25/40 (Acceptable)
27	
28	| # | Heuristic | Score | Key Issue |
29	|---|-----------|-------|-----------|
30	| 1 | Visibility of System Status | 2 | Image invisible while loading; silent /info failure |
31	| 2 | Match System / Real World | 4 | -- |
32	| 3 | User Control and Freedom | 3 | Focus mode exits work (Esc, overlay) |
33	| 4 | Consistency and Standards | 3 | Animated-bottom-border reused cleanly |
34	| 5 | Error Prevention | 3 | -- |
35	| 6 | Recognition Rather Than Recall | 2 | Focus toggle unlabeled; copy affordance subtle |
36	| 7 | Flexibility and Efficiency | 1 | No keyboard shortcuts; single path |
37	| 8 | Aesthetic and Minimalist Design | 3 | 10rem dead zone undermines minimalism |
38	| 9 | Error Recovery | 2 | `.catch(() => {})` on /info -- zero feedback |
39	| 10 | Help and Documentation | 2 | Endpoint list is only docs |
40	
41	Cognitive load checklist: 1 failure (low, good).
42	
43	## What's Working
44	
45	1. **Image is the hero** -- fills ~80vh on desktop, everything recedes. Focus mode ("dim the lights") with 1.5s transition is cinematic and on-brand.
46	2. **Usage row nails the pitch** -- "New day, new photo, same URL" + copyable URL + img tag. Entire value prop in two lines. Copy interaction with "Copied" badge provides real feedback.
47	3. **Typography is distinctive** -- Source Serif/Sans/Code Pro family creates hierarchy through subtlety, not volume.
48	
49	## Priority Issues
50

52	Creates massive scroll void on desktop between usage row and endpoints. Users think the page ends. Endpoints section uses `.fade-up` (opacity: 0) and IntersectionObserver may never fire if nobody scrolls through the void.
53	**Fix**: Reduce to 3-4rem.
54	**Command**: `/arrange`

9	# Serve OG HTML to social crawlers on api.nasapicture.com
10	
11	## Problem
12	
13	Twitter/Facebook/etc. link previews need an HTML page with Open Graph meta tags. When their crawlers hit `api.nasapicture.com/`, the Worker responds with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` (the raw APOD image), so there's no HTML to parse and no card renders. This means tweets linking `api.nasapicture.com` show no preview image.
14	
15	## Fix
16	
17	In the Worker, sniff the `User-Agent` header on incoming requests to the image routes. If the UA matches a known social crawler, return an HTML document with OG tags instead of the image bytes. Otherwise, behave as today and return the image.
18	
19	## Affected routes
20	
21	The crawler check should run before the image response for these route groups in `src/index.ts`:
22	
23	- `hdPaths`: `/`, `/image.jpg`
24	- `sdPaths`: `/sd`, `/image-sd.jpg`
25	- `optimizedPaths`: `/optimized`, `/image-optimized.jpg`
26	- `thumbPaths`: `/thumb`, `/thumb.jpg`
27	
28	The `/info` and `/about` routes already return text, so they don't need this.
29	
30	## Implementation approach
31	
32	1. **Add a `isSocialCrawler(request)` helper** that reads `User-Agent` and tests against a regex of known crawler substrings (case-insensitive).
33	
34	2. **Add a `buildOgHtml(apod, requestUrl)` helper** that takes the APOD metadata (already fetched by `findLatestImage`) and the request URL, and returns a minimal HTML string with OG tags.
35	
36	3. **Insert the check early in each image route block**, after `findLatestImage` resolves but before fetching the upstream image. If it's a crawler, return the OG HTML and skip the image fetch entirely (saves bandwidth and latency).
37	
38	```
39	if (isSocialCrawler(request)) {
40	  const apod = await findLatestImage(log, apiKey);
41	  res = new Response(buildOgHtml(apod, reqUrl), {
42	    headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" }),
43	  });
44	}
45	```
46	
47	Since `findLatestImage` is already called for these routes, the crawler path just skips the image fetch/transform step.
48	
49	## Crawler User-Agents to match (case-insensitive substring)
50	
51	- `Twitterbot`
52	- `facebookexternalhit`
53	- `Facebot`
54	- `Slackbot`
55	- `Discordbot`
56	- `LinkedInBot`
57	- `TelegramBot`
58	- `WhatsApp`
59	- `Pinterest`
60	- `redditbot`
61	
62	## HTML response shape
63	
64	Minimal document with:
65	
66	- `<title>` — APOD title + "| nasapicture.com"
67	- `<meta name="description">` — truncated APOD explanation
68	- `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type=website`, `og:url`
69	- `og:image` — `https://api.nasapicture.com/sd` (standard res is more reliable for card dimensions)
70	- `og:image:width` / `og:image:height` — from `fetchImageDimensions` if available, omit if not
71	- `og:site_name` — "nasapicture.com"
72	- `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`
73	
74	## Caching consideration
75	
76	Crawler responses can use the same cache TTL as regular image responses. The OG HTML is date-keyed (same APOD metadata), so it rolls over at midnight ET like everything else. Consider using a distinct cache key suffix (e.g., `:og`) to avoid serving HTML from the image cache or vice versa.
77	
78	## Testing
79	
80	- Use `curl -A "Twitterbot/1.0"` to verify the crawler path returns HTML
81	- Use `curl` with no special UA to verify normal image behavior is unchanged
82	- Validate the returned HTML with the [Twitter Card Validator](https://cards-dev.twitter.com/validator) and [Facebook Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/)
83
```

8	
9	# Generate a daily OG image
10	
11	Generate a new Open Graph image every day, resized and cropped to the optimal 1200x630px dimensions. Adding a text overlay with the logo would be a bonus.
12	
13	## Context
14	
15	The current OG image points to `https://api.nasapicture.com/image.jpg`, which serves the raw APOD at whatever dimensions NASA provides (often square or portrait). Social platforms expect 1200x630px for optimal previews.
16	
17	## Recommended approach: `workers-og`
18	
19	[`workers-og`](https://github.com/kvnang/workers-og) renders HTML/CSS to PNG entirely inside a Worker (Satori → SVG → PNG, no browser needed). This is purpose-built for OG image generation at the edge.
20	
21	**How it would work:**
22	1. Add a `/og` route to the existing Worker (or a separate one)
23	2. Fetch today's APOD metadata from `/info` (title, date)
24	3. Render an HTML template with the APOD photo as background, title text, and nasapicture.com branding
25	4. Cache the result aggressively (24h TTL keyed to date) — one cold generation per day
26	5. Update the `og:image` meta tag to point to the new `/og` route
27	
28	**Pros:** Single Worker, zero external dependencies, familiar HTML/CSS for layout, no billing (stays within free Workers tier since we're generating the image ourselves, not using Cloudflare's Images API).
29	
30	**Cons:** Satori supports flexbox only (no CSS grid). Custom fonts need to be embedded as ArrayBuffers (adds to bundle size). Subset of CSS supported.
31	
32	## Alternative: Cloudflare Images binding
33	
34	Use the Images binding (`env.IMAGES`) to resize/crop the APOD to 1200x630 natively, then `.draw()` a pre-rendered text overlay PNG on top.
35	
36	- Requires `[images] binding = "IMAGES"` in `wrangler.toml`
37	- Free tier: 5,000 unique transformations/month (we'd use ~30/month — well within limits)
38	- Higher-fidelity resizing with smart crop/gravity options
39	- More moving parts (two-step: resize + composite)
40	
41	This is the upgrade path if `workers-og` quality isn't sufficient or if we need smarter cropping (e.g. face/subject detection).
42	
43	## Not viable
44	
45	- **Sharp** — uses native Node.js modules, incompatible with Workers
46	- **Canvas APIs** — no browser context in Workers
47	
48	## Useful links
49	
50	- [workers-og](https://github.com/kvnang/workers-og)
51	- [@cf-wasm/photon](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cf-wasm/photon) — WASM image processing if more control is needed
52	- [Cloudflare Images: draw overlays](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/transform-images/draw-overlays/)
53	- [Cloudflare Images pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/pricing/) — free up to 5,000 transformations/month
54
```

9	
10	# Add GitHub Action to auto-deploy to Cloudflare on PR merge into main
11	
12	Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that runs `npm run deploy` automatically when a PR is merged into `main`. This removes the manual deploy step after each merge.
13	
14	## Current Deploy Process
15	
16	`npm run deploy` runs two steps sequentially:
17	1. `deploy:api` — `wrangler deploy` (Worker to `api.nasapicture.com` + `get.nasapicture.com`)
18	2. `deploy:landing` — `vite build` + `wrangler pages deploy landing/dist/ --project-name nasapicture-landing`
19	
20	## Implementation Plan
21	
22	### 1. Create `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
23	
24	**Trigger**: `push` to `main` (covers PR merges and direct pushes)
25	
26	**Jobs**: Single job with these steps:
27	1. Checkout repo
28	2. Set up Node.js (LTS, e.g. 22.x) — add `.nvmrc` to pin version
29	3. `npm ci` (root deps: wrangler, typescript, workers-types)
30	4. `npm ci --prefix landing` (landing deps: vite, sass)
31	5. `npx tsc --noEmit` — type-check gate, fail the deploy if types are broken
32	6. `npm run deploy` — deploys both Worker and Pages
33	
34	### 2. GitHub Repository Secrets Required
35	
36	| Secret | Purpose |
37	|---|---|
38	| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Wrangler auth for both Worker and Pages deploys |
39	| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | Target Cloudflare account |
40	
41	The API token needs permissions: **Workers Scripts: Edit**, **Cloudflare Pages: Edit**, and **Account Settings: Read**.
42	
43	`NASA_API_KEY` is already set via `wrangler secret` on the Worker itself, so it does not need to be in GitHub secrets.
44	
45	### 3. Add `.nvmrc`
46	
47	Pin Node.js version (e.g. `22`) at the repo root so the workflow and local dev stay in sync.
48	
49	## Workflow Skeleton
50	
51	```yaml
52	name: Deploy
53	on:
54	  push:
55	    branches: [main]
56	
57	jobs:
58	  deploy:
59	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
60	    steps:
61	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
62	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
63	        with:
64	          node-version-file: .nvmrc
65	          cache: npm
66	      - run: npm ci
67	      - run: npm ci --prefix landing
68	      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
69	      - run: npm run deploy
70	        env:
71	          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
72	          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
73	```
74	
75	## Considerations
76	
77	- **Single job vs. split jobs**: A single job is simpler and the total deploy is fast (type-check + wrangler deploy + pages deploy). No need to parallelize until it becomes slow.
78	- **No deploy on non-main branches**: Dev/feature branches never trigger deploys, matching the existing "deploy from main only" rule.
79	- **Failure notifications**: GitHub sends email on workflow failure by default, which is sufficient. Slack/webhook notifications can be added later if needed.
80	- **Caching**: `actions/setup-node` with `cache: npm` caches `~/.npm` across runs, speeding up installs.
81	- **Pages deploy**: `wrangler pages deploy` uses the same `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, no separate Pages token needed.
82
```
</details></tool-use>

9	# Local timezone APOD rollover
10	
11	Users might find it useful (both in the API and the landing page) to choose to get the new image at midnight in their local timezone, instead of when it actually rolls over in ET.
12	
13	## The problem
14	
15	APOD publishes once per day, keyed to Eastern Time. A user in Tokyo (UTC+9) sees the image roll over at 1pm JST -- awkward if they want "a new picture every morning." Conversely, a user in PST sees it change at 9pm, which might actually be fine.
16	
17	## Possible API surface
18	
19	A query parameter like `?tz=Asia/Tokyo` or `?tz=UTC%2B9` on any image endpoint. The Worker would compute "today" in the requested timezone instead of ET, and request that date's APOD.
20	
21	## Key constraint
22	
23	If a user's local date is ahead of ET (e.g., it's April 2 in Tokyo but still April 1 in ET), the April 2 APOD doesn't exist yet. The Worker would need to fall back to the most recent available date, which is what `findLatestImage` already does via lookback. So this might mostly work out of the box -- the timezone param just changes which date the lookback starts from.
24	
25	## Landing page
26	
27	Could detect timezone via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` and pass it to the API. Or let users toggle between "NASA time" and "local time" if we want to keep it explicit.
28	
29	## Phasing
30	
31	Nice-to-have, not critical. Phase 1 could just handle timezones behind ET (west of Eastern), which is straightforward -- the requested date always exists. Timezones ahead of ET (where the date might not exist yet) can come later if there's demand.
32	
33	## Related
34	
35	Ties naturally into TASK-0011 (R2 storage layer for image archiving). If we're storing the last N images anyway, serving a timezone-shifted "yesterday" from the archive is trivial. Any tasks spawned from this note are likely blocked by TASK-0011.
36	
37	## Open questions
38	
39	- Caching implications: timezone-varied requests would reduce cache hit rates since each timezone produces a different date key during the rollover window
40
```
</details></tool-use>

10	# Add a user-facing gallery of past APOD images
11	
12	A browsable archive/gallery showing past Astronomy Pictures of the Day. Depends on TASK-0011 (R2 storage layer) being in place to persist historical images.
13	
14	## Why
15	
16	The daily APOD is ephemeral by design, but visitors naturally want to browse past images. A gallery turns the site from a single-serving utility into something worth revisiting. NASA's own APOD archive is functional but not visually engaging, so there's room to offer a better browsing experience that matches the project's aesthetic.
17	
18	## Data available from R2
19	
20	TASK-0011 defines the R2 key structure as:
21	
22	- `{date}/hd.{ext}` — HD image
23	- `{date}/sd.{ext}` — SD image
24	- `{date}/info.json` — metadata snapshot (title, explanation, copyright, dimensions)
25	
26	The `info.json` sidecar gives us everything we need for gallery cards without hitting NASA's API. The archive builds organically from the day R2 goes live, one image per day.
27	
28	## API surface
29	
30	The gallery needs a way to list and fetch archived images. Options:
31	
32	- **New route: `/archive`** — returns JSON listing of available dates (from R2 `list()`)
33	- **New route: `/archive/{date}`** — returns image for a specific date (from R2)
34	- **New route: `/archive/{date}/info`** — returns metadata for a specific date
35	
36	Alternatively, the existing `/info?date=2026-04-01` could accept a date param. But dedicated archive routes are cleaner and avoid overloading the "today" endpoints.
37	
38	## Frontend
39	
40	### Location
41	Could live on the landing page as a section below the hero, or as a dedicated `/gallery` page. A separate page avoids bloating the clean single-page landing, and gives room for richer browsing UX.
42	
43	### Layout ideas
44	- Thumbnail grid using Cloudflare Image Transformations (same approach as `/thumb` route, but per-date)
45	- Click/tap to expand with title, explanation, and full-res image
46	- Date-based navigation (calendar picker or month groupings)
47	- Infinite scroll or paginated grid
48	
49	### Performance
50	- Grid thumbnails via `cf.image` transforms (small, blurred placeholders with lazy-loaded sharper versions)
51	- Pre-sized containers using dimensions from `info.json` (same pattern as the current hero image)
52	- Paginate R2 `list()` calls to avoid loading the entire archive at once
53	
54	## Related board items
55	
56	- **TASK-0011** (blocker): R2 storage layer that archives images and metadata daily
57	- **EPIC-0002**: Landing page polish, gallery would be a major addition under this umbrella
58	- **NOTE-0005**: Individual metadata routes (`/title`, `/date`, etc.) could extend to per-date variants
59	- **NOTE-0008**: Daily OG image generation, could reuse the gallery's per-date image serving
60	- **NOTE-0016**: Local timezone rollover also depends on R2 and date-keyed image access
61	
62	## Open questions
63	
64	- Gallery on the landing page or a separate `/gallery` route?
65	- How far back to go? Only from when R2 archiving starts, or backfill older images from NASA's API?
66	- Search/filter by title or keyword, or just date-based browsing?
67	- Should the gallery be part of the Cloudflare Pages landing site, or served by the Worker?

9	# Add a "Why is this needed" section to the landing page
10	
11	Add a short content block between the hero image and the endpoint docs that explains what APOD is and what nasapicture.com solves. Spawned from NOTE-0006.
12	
13	## What to cover
14	
15	- **What is APOD?** NASA has published a new Astronomy Picture of the Day every day since 1995, each with a professional explanation from astronomers.
16	- **The problem.** NASA's API requires a key, rate-limits (30 req/hr on DEMO_KEY), sometimes returns videos instead of images, and doesn't offer a single stable URL that always points to "today's image."
17	- **What this solves.** A fixed URL that always returns today's image, no API key, no rate limits (edge-cached), no video days (auto-fallback). Drop it in an `<img>` tag.
18	
19	## Tone and placement
20	
21	- Concise, a few short paragraphs. Match the existing voice: clever, minimal, precise.
22	- Place between the hero image and the developer route docs so non-technical visitors get context before the technical details.

24

28	- Reads naturally to a non-technical visitor
